answer: A stake-bonded registry makes each agent identity cost real money: to join, an agent locks a deposit, like a marble placed on the table, and the bond is slashed if the agent is caught cheating. One honest agent pays once, but a Sybil attacker must fund thousands of deposits, so forging an army becomes ruinously expensive. Reputation then accrues slowly, like velvet wearing smooth only with use, and new identities start at the jetty: able to dock, but trusted with nothing valuable until they prove themselves over time.
